chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad, from Yunus, who said:

I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who leased land or other property from a man for a specified number of years. Then the lessor wanted to sell his land which he had leased out before the expiration of the specified term. Is it for the lessee to prevent him from the sale before the expiration of the term for which he leased it from him to him, and what is obligated for the lessee for it? He (peace be upon him) wrote to him: He may sell if he stipulates upon the buyer that for the lessee would be from the years what was (contracted) for him.
ai.seo_question: Can a landlord sell a property that is currently leased, and what happens to the tenant's rights?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) establishes that the sale of leased property does not invalidate the existing lease, a principle known as 'al-bay' yata'abbad al-'aqd' (the sale does not break the contract). It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on protecting the lessee's possession rights against new owners, ensuring contractual stability in property transactions.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ahmad, from Yunus who said,

‘I wrote to Al Rea<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who leased a land or other than that from a man for a specified number of years. Then the land owner wanted to sell his land which he had leased out before the expiration of the specified term. It is for the lessee that he prevent him from the sale before the expiration of his term which it had been lease from him to him, and what obligated the lessee for it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘For him is to sell when he stipulates upon the buyer that for the lessee would be from the years what were (contracted) for him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Ahmad from Yunus who has said the following:

‘I once wrote to al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked about the case of a man who formed a contract with another man about land or something else for several known years and the landlord then decided to sell the land before the end of the contract; if the tenant could stop the sale before the end of the time of agreement and if so, what was the tenant’s responsibility. He (the Imam) wrote back the answer that said, ’He can sell it if he sets a condition upon the buyer that requires him to allow the tenant to use his years according to the contract of tenancy.’”
